_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for JBM Auto. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

industry.components: JBM's component division sells sheet-metal assemblies, chassis and suspension parts, tanks and exhausts to Indian car, utility-vehicle and truck makers. Its growth follows Indian vehicle output and content per vehicle: segment revenue grew from Rs1,455 cr (FY20) to Rs3,443 cr (FY26), 15.4% a year, but only 8% in FY26 before picking up to 15.5% in Q1FY27 as car demand recovered after the Sep-2025 GST cut (AR FY26 MD&A).
industry.ebus: India's e-bus market is driven by government programmes: more than 90% of e-bus sales go to state transport undertakings, mostly on gross cost contracts (GCC), where a private operator buys, runs and maintains the buses and the city pays a fee per kilometre for 10-12 years. Industry e-bus sales rose from ~1,200 (FY22) to ~4,900 (FY26) (KPMG, cited in AR FY26). Programmes: PM e-Bus Sewa (10,000 buses in tier-2/3 cities; 6,862 sanctioned and 5,195 deployed by Jan-2026), PM E-DRIVE (14,028 buses for nine large cities; 13,800 allocated by Mar-2026; Rs1,500 cr in the FY27 budget), state programmes; awards of ~46,000 e-buses are due for deployment over 2-3 years (AR FY26 MD&A).
industry.competition: E-bus makers include Switch Mobility (Ashok Leyland), Olectra Greentech and JBM. JBM claims ~24% of FY26 sales (1,282 buses) and ~25% in Q1FY27; VAHAN data reported in the press put it second in FY26 after Switch.
industry.gcc: The GCC model makes the operator, not the city, carry the capital: the operator funds the buses up front, recovers the cost over 10-12 years from city payments, and depends on payment-security mechanisms. JBM both makes the buses and, through its JV JBM Ecolife, runs them: the group's sales are only as good as Ecolife's funding. IFC's Sep-2025 investment came with a payment-security mechanism meant to reduce city payment risk.
industry.src: AR FY26 MD&A (KPMG, PIB sources cited there); Crisil 5-Aug-2026; IFC 11-Sep-2025

excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: exceptional charges in three of the last four quarters (Rs358 cr in Jun-2026, which turned the quarter into a loss), so its ~93x trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on depressed EPS (same exclusion as the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda, Sona and Craftsman initiations).
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring), so there is no five-year median (same exclusion as the other auto-component initiations).

street._note: Coverage is thin. No broker note dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 could be found: Trendlyne's research list for JBM Auto ends in Sep-2020 (Dolat Capital, Buy, Rs373 pre-split), the company holds no earnings calls, and press coverage of the Q1FY27 results (30-Jul-2026) and of the Bain report (21-Aug-2026) quotes no broker target. Web pages that list broker targets for JBM Auto without dates, methods or a publication date on or before our as-of date, and aggregator consensus figures that do not name brokers, are not used.
street.methodView: With no dated broker notes, we value JBM Auto the way the market quotes it and the way the house values auto-component makers: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (Sep-28E). A sum-of-the-parts (components on P/E, e-buses on EV/EBITDA) is the natural alternative, but no note on or before 30-Sep-2026 uses it and the e-bus economics are split between JBM Auto (manufacturing, 85% owned) and the equity-accounted JV JBM Ecolife (operations), whose accounts are not disclosed; we do not build one. Olectra Greentech's P/E is shown as a sensitivity.

ownership.trend: Promoters have held 67.53% in every quarter since Dec-2023; FIIs fell from 3.3% (Mar-2024) to ~2%; domestic institutions hold almost nothing (0.16%); shareholders grew from ~89,000 (Dec-2023) to ~183,000 (Jun-2026): a retail-owned stock.

stockEvents.what: All-time high Rs1,102 (split-adjusted): ~46x in four years on the e-bus story; forward P/E above 100x.
Rs592: down 46% from the peak as FY25 growth slowed to 9%.
Rs693 after the Motilal Oswal investment in JBM Ecolife.
Up ~10% intraday to Rs685 on the Bain Capital report; JBM said no binding agreement.

moat.components: Long relationships with Tata Motors, M&M and VECV; tooling in-house (the Tool Room's 18-20% EBIT margin is the best business in the group). But sheet-metal parts are a competitive, build-to-print business with many listed and unlisted suppliers: component EBIT margin 3-8% over FY20-26 (segment notes).
moat.ebus: Scale (~20,000-bus capacity, the largest e-bus plant outside China by its own description), ~24-25% share, a full range (city, intercity, coach, sleeper, tarmac) and the integration of manufacturing with its own operator. The catch: much of the demand it serves is its own JV's, funded with group money, and tenders are won on price per kilometre.
moat.verdict: No durable moat in components; a scale lead in e-buses that rests on government tenders and on the group's willingness to finance its own customer.

critiques: Receivables doubled to Rs2,185 cr and contract assets reached Rs1,511 cr in FY26 while revenue grew 11%: revenue is recognised as buses are built, and much of it is owed by the group's own JV.
The EV business earned Rs251 cr of segment EBIT on Rs5,129 cr of segment assets in FY26 (4.9%): it consumes capital faster than it earns profit.
JBM Auto funds its customer: Rs336 cr of loans, Rs302 cr of preference shares and guarantees to JBM Ecolife and its SPVs at Mar-26.
Other income tripled to Rs139 cr in FY26, mostly interest from the JV and a Rs36 cr miscellaneous line: about a third of PBT.
The 15% minority in JBM Electric Vehicles and possible stake sales in the EV business (Bain reports) mean shareholders own less of the growth than the consolidated revenue suggests.
No earnings calls, no investor presentations we could find, no order-book reconciliation: the disclosure is thin for a Rs13,000 cr company.
Promoters own 67.5%; institutions own ~2%; the stock has been retail-driven (Rs24 to Rs1,102 to Rs557 in six years).
gaps: Broker notes: none dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 were found; the street table is empty and the consensus is not shown.
Related-party sales to JBM Ecolife and its SPVs: the AR FY26 note 51 is printed as rotated tables our text extraction could not read reliably; not quantified.
JBM Ecolife's own accounts (revenue, debt, fleet, losses) and the terms of the Motilal Oswal and IFC instruments (valuation, coupon, conversion): not disclosed in our sources.
Quarterly segment EBIT for Q1FY26 and Q2FY26 (only H1FY26) and all FY25 quarters: not collected.
Bus volumes other than FY26 (~1,282) and the order book in rupees after FY25 (Rs12,900 cr): not disclosed.
Jun-2026 balance sheet: not published (half-yearly); we use Mar-26 pro forma for the Rs410 cr upstreaming.
Named non-promoter holders for Jun-2026: not available.
conflicts: E-bus rank in FY26: the company says #1 with ~24% (1,282 buses, AR FY26); press reports of VAHAN data put JBM second after Switch Mobility. We say 'one of the two largest'.

Order book: 'over 11,000 buses' (Feb-2025 and AR FY25), '10,000+ deployed and under execution' (Jun-2026), and 7,000-7,500 to be executed over 2-3 years (Crisil, Aug-2026). The first two include buses already deployed; we use Crisil's figure for execution.

Debt: Crisil Rs3,204 cr at Mar-26 (its adjusted basis); Screener Rs3,029 cr; long-term debt cut 'Rs500 cr approx.' (press release) vs Rs400-420 cr upstreamed (Crisil). We use Screener's figure and Rs410 cr.
Revenue FY26: Crisil Rs5,941 cr (adjusted); reported Rs6,088 cr. We use reported.
